summary.short: Budget accountability statute approving the 2017 Rendición de Cuentas. Its few data and labour provisions apply Law 18.331 to certain foreign controllers, require breach notices, data protection officers, and an annual report on automation and jobs. Generally in force from 1 January 2019.
summary.long: Approves the 2017 Rendición de Cuentas and budget execution balance (Art. 1). Most of the provided text reallocates budget credits and creates or suppresses posts across ministries. Its data-related provisions are operative. Art. 37 extends the personal data law (Ley 18.331) to controllers not established in Uruguay where processing relates to offering goods or services to inhabitants or analysing their behaviour, or uses means located in the country. Art. 38 requires controllers to notify data subjects and the Unidad Reguladora y de Control de Datos Personales of security breaches. Art. 40 requires data protection officers in public entities and some private entities. Art. 41 requires an annual executive report on the employment impact of automation, supported by a risk and opportunity matrix of jobs over five-year periods. Arts. 81 and 97 impose device-identification and location-data duties on mobile and telecom operators. Art. 194 creates an electronic clinical history with a patient right to oppose access. Unless a provision states otherwise, the law applies from 1 January 2019. The text sets no separate sanctions for the data provisions.
